items.title: Stocks Erase Post-Midterm Elections Rally, Dragged Down by Tech
items.description: The S&P 500 slumped to its worst daily decline since April 2025 and the tech-heavy Nasdaq entered correction territory, as investors fretted about the durability of the A.I. build-out.

items.title: Tech Billionaires Face Tricky Political Waters After Democratic Midterm Sweep
items.description: Many donated money to President Trump’s favored causes and became his allies. Now that political alignment may be a liability.

items.title: Trump Tried to Undermine the Nation’s Elections. It Didn’t Work.
items.description: Millions of Americans cast their ballots on Tuesday in an election that showed the resiliency of democracy. The president said he would accept the results.

items.title: U.S. Finds Subdued Foreign Meddling Operations in Midterm Elections
items.description: Russia was linked to influence campaigns targeting Democrats that gained little traction, but the Kremlin may be more focused on France’s elections in the spring.

items.title: Why a Merciless Supreme Court Rebuke on Election Eve Matters
items.description: The justices took just hours to reject Trump’s bid to meddle in the election.

items.title: The Evening: The Blue Wave Swells
items.description: Plus, Gov. Gavin Newsom clears California’s death row. Here’s the latest at the end of Thursday.

items.title: The Machine, and the Messaging, That Won Texas for Democrats
items.description: Years of organizing met a moment of voter discontent, as James Talarico and Gina Hinojosa offered Texans a vision of economic relief and political change.

items.title: How Democrats Won Across the South
items.description: They won Senate races in North Carolina, South Carolina and Georgia, with a Mississippi race still too close to call. Their wins lifted down-ballot candidates too.

items.title: In Alaska, Ranked-Choice Ballots Are Unlikely to Be Enough for Dan Sullivan
items.description: An analysis shows Mary Peltola is likely to keep her lead in the Senate race in part because of ballots she’d accumulate in ranked-choice tabulation from supporters of the other Dan Sullivan.

items.title: Across the South, Black Voters Help Propel Democratic Wins
items.description: Democrats in the South used anger over redistricting, cuts to key federal programs and attacks on Black history to help galvanize a crucial bloc of voters to the polls.

items.title: Newsom Commutes the Sentences of California’s 548 Death Row Inmates

items.title: Up in the Clouds With the Pope, It’s Still Commercial
items.description: Unlike American presidents, Pope Leo XIV has no private jet, so he travels on commercial airlines, like the rest of us. Well, almost.

items.title: DOJ Steps Up Leak Investigation on Supreme Court Decision Overturning Roe v. Wade
items.description: Investigators, using subpoenas and other law enforcement powers, are accelerating an inquiry that takes the Trump administration into the inner workings of the court.

items.title: Justice Alito Will Not Retire From Supreme Court Immediately, Despite Election Outcome
items.description: The conservative justice has told friends he does not plan to step down before the end of the court’s term, even as Democrats are set to seize the Senate in January.

items.title: Harmeet Dhillon, Leader of Justice Department’s Civil Rights Unit, Resigns
items.description: The move came after conflicts with Justice Department leaders, including disagreements over legal strategy in the midterm elections, people familiar with the matter said.
